the FL-P cell synapses in the parvoccullar MVN/Prh are mainly formed on relatively small-diameter distal dendrites and that the synapses of vestibulo-nerve and those of FL P-celled closely apposed each other on these dendrites, suggesting that the FL P-cells can inhibit the vestibulo-ocular reflex by inhibiting the vestibulo-nerverve synaptic transmission.

the FL P-cell synapses on the parvocellar MVN/Prh neurons are mainly formed on relatively small-diameter distal dendrites, often closely apposed to those of vestibular nerves, suggesting that inhibitory synapse of FL P-celis may influence the function on the excitatory synapses in the parvocal MVN/Prf neurons.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the FL P-cells mainly terminate on somata and the proximal dendrites in the magnocelluar MVN, and on relatively small-diameter dendrites in the border region between the parvocelluar MVNs and the PrH.
FL P-cell axon terminals are mainly distributed in the magneto- and parvocellular regions of the MVN, where they form synapses mainly on somata and dendrites of glutamatergics neurons, respectively.

the synapses of cerebellar FL P-cells terminate on the somata and proximo-dendritic regions of magnocellular MVNs and on the distal dendritic regions of parvocelluar MVNs, forming symmetrical inhibitory synapses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the FL P-cell synapses are located in both the magnocellular and parvocellular regions of the MVN, and the synapses in the parvocalular MVN/Prh may influence the vestibular nerve synapses on the same MVN neurons.

the FL P-cell synaptic inputs onto the parvocellular MVN/Prh neurons may play a role in short-term adaptation, and the vestibular nerve synaptic inputs onto the same parvocelluar MVN/Pr H neurons may play a more important role in long-term adaptation.
the cerebellum-dependent vestibulo-ocular adaptation may involve the plasticity of the FL P-cell synapses on the glutamatergical parvocellular neurons of the MVN.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the FL-MVN pathway is likely to be involved in the vestibulo-ocular adaptation, which has been suggested by physiological and pharmacological experiments, and that the FL synapses may influence the vestibular synaptic inputs to the MVN.
the FL-MVN synaptic circuit may play an important role in the cerebellum-dependent adaptation of vestibulo-oculomotor system.
the FL P-cell synapses are distributed in the magnonuclear and border region of the magnocellular and parvocellular vestibular nuclei, where the FL-targeted MVN and PrH neurons are located.
